newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen firmer on aggressive bids.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen firmer on aggressive bids.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were expected to end firmer from Thursday levels on aggressive bids, traders said.
Traders expected 180-cst supplies for October lifting from Singapore to be quoted around $117 per tonne on a free-on-board basis. This is firmer from Thursday's bid/asked at $115/$117 per tonne.
Cash levels also firmed despite losses seen on crudes and lower paper swaps quotes, traders said.
In the swaps market, October was quoted at $115.25/$115.75, lower from $116-$117 per tonne seen on Thursday.
Traders said a major oil company and a trader were bidding agressively. They said the return of Chinese demand has also helped to boost levels.
Chinese bids were heard ranging between $122 and $124 a tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to South China, traders said.
Already five cargoes were heard to have been sold into China between end September and late October, a trader said.
